In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of age on the uterotrophic action of estrogen and on estrogen-progesterone interrelationships in immature and adult animals.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the immature rat estrogen pretreatment decreases uterine uptake and metabolism of tritiated-progesterone.

the effects of estradiol pretreatment on progesterone uptake and metabolism in the rat uterus are complex and variable, and are not easily related to the age of the animal or the dose of progesterone.
the uptake of progesterone by the immature uterus is greater than in the adult uterus and that this is not a consequence of estrogen-induced uterine growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the uterus is not a passive organ in the regulation of the progesterone-estrogen balance.
the uterus of immature rats, but not of mature rats, has a capacity to metabolize progesterone to a greater extent than the brain.
the effects of estrogen in uterus and brain are dependent on the age, the duration of estrogen treatment and the dose of progesterone.
The main takeaway from our work is that

estrogen can inhibit progesterone uptake in the uterus of immature but not adult rats and that the inhibition is not due to estrogen-induced changes in uterine weight or uterotrophic response to estradiol.
the brain is a target organ for estrogen.
the effects of estrogen on progesterone uptake and metabolism are age-dependent and may be mediated through a mechanism other than estrogen-induced uterotropic effects.
